original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-H0-L-morphism-ringed-topoi}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. Then $H^0(L_f) = \Omega_f$.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-triangle-ringed-topoi}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}_1), \mathcal{O}_1) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}_2), \mathcal{O}_2)$ and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}_2), \mathcal{O}_2) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}_3), \mathcal{O}_3)$ be morphisms of ringed topoi.
Then there is a canonical distinguished triangle
$$
Lf^* L_g \to L_{g \circ f} \to L_f \to Lf^*L_g[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_1)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-cotangent-complex-with-naive-ringed-topoi}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. There is a canonical map $L_f \to \NL_f$ which
identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
$\tau_{\geq -1}L_f$.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheafified two-term complex $(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P}\mathcal B)$ in degrees $-1,0$, where locally $\mathcal P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ is a polynomial algebra presentation with kernel $\mathcal I$. The canonical comparison identifies this complex with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ in the derived category.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. There is a canonical map $L_f \to \mathrm{NL}_f$ which
identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
$\tau_{\geq -1}L_f$.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves ringed-topos comparison L_f→NL_f and identifies its degree ≥−1 truncation with the naive two-term cotangent complex, without overclaiming full quasi-isomorphism.
